# Review of E1 (Q-1 and G-1), ticket DAEO-sdxk, independent-auditor

Reviewed: commit 04568e140703 on emg/queue (merge_queue.py, README, test_merge_queue_q1.py) and tools/land.candidate.py
against land.py, with test_land_dec1050.py. Judged by ADR-0001's threat model and the two questions of JUDGEMENT.md.

Tests run through heavy_slot.sh: test_merge_queue_q1.py 21 passed; test_land_dec1050.py 22 passed.

## G-1 probes (throwaway repositories, acceptance_authors called directly)
Flagged correctly: plain commit with Role: engineer; no Role trailer; mixed roles (designer plus engineer); deletion of an
acceptance file; rename out of it; mode-only change; a merge that keeps the first parent and drops the designer's change
(`-s ours`); a merge that resolves a conflict in an acceptance file; a merge with a hand edit in it (two parents); an
octopus merge (counted whether or not it changes anything of its own, conservative); a Role trailer in a non-final
paragraph (refused, fails closed). Not flagged, correctly: a clean merge of w2/integrate into the branch (its commits are
outside the range); a clean merge of the designer's branch (the designer's commits are judged one by one). A missing
w2/integrate refuses with a named git failure. A refusal happens before anything is enqueued, so no tree or queue state is
touched.

## Q-1 reading
trace_once, the same-failure rule (types of the failure, both lists non-empty and equal), the nightly "passed" step first,
the 3 rounds only for the list, the refresh-or-rebuild path (refresh only while the branch is still at the head; else one
seeded rebuild; a failed rebuild is a Stop that keeps the entries) all read as specified. Non-0/1 exits and timeouts on the
head side count as the batch's (an ejection, never a clearing): they fail closed.

## F1 (G-1): a merge that changes an acceptance file with a non-ASCII or otherwise quoted name is not counted
Behaviour: for a two-parent merge, `log --remerge-diff --name-only` and, for an octopus, `diff --name-only` print names
with special characters quoted (core.quotepath), for example `"tests/acceptance/\303\251.py"`. The code tests
`n.startswith("tests/acceptance/")`, which is false for the quoted form. A merge commit whose own change there is such a
file is left out, and the landing passes with no designer role. Plain commits are not affected (they go through rev-list's
path limit). Fix: `-z` with a NUL split (or `-c core.quotepath=off`).
Reproduce: in a repository, merge a branch with `--no-commit`, add `tests/acceptance/<e-acute>.py`, commit with Role:
engineer; `acceptance_authors(HEAD)` returns `([], n)` with n counting only the designer's commits. Confirmed.
Severity: low. It needs a merge with a hand edit that also carries a quoted file name.
Ordinary work: no, because it needs an edit made inside a merge commit and a non-ASCII (or tab or quote) file name in the
acceptance folder; the same edit as a plain commit, or with an ASCII name, is refused.
Consequence: fails open
Scope: in (G-1). A row for the Wave 3 hardening pass; the fix is one flag.

## F2 (Q-1): the same-failure memo `seen` is never reset between passes and unions kinds
Behaviour: `self.seen[(clone, case)]` accumulates failure types over the whole run. With --warm the clone path is the same
in a later pass (after an ejection and a re-merge). If a case was red with type A in pass 1, and in pass 2 its alone re-run
is a timeout (rc 1, no JUnit, so no kinds), kw still reads {A}; a head-side red of type A then clears it as not the batch's.
Reproduce: not constructed; read from the code (merge_queue.py `alone` and `seen_kinds`, lines 696 to 706 and 810).
Severity: low; needs a timeout of exactly that case in a later pass.
Ordinary work: no, because it needs a red, an ejection, then a timeout of the same case in the next pass, and the head
side red with the same type.
Consequence: fails open
Scope: in (Q-1). Row for Wave 3; the fix is to clear `seen` entries of a clone at each fresh merge.

## F3 (Q-1): "same failure" is the exception type only
Behaviour: a case red on the head with AssertionError and red with the batch with AssertionError for another reason is
cleared as unowned. This is the earlier rule (DEC-989) kept as it was; one run each way is less evidence than the earlier
3 rounds, but the rule itself did not change.
Severity: low, and unchanged by E1.
Ordinary work: no, because the case must already be red on the head with the same type, and a head with a known red is
investigated at once (DEC-968).
Consequence: fails open
Scope: out (not changed by Q-1).

## F4 (Q-1): an infrastructure failure on the head side blames the batch
Behaviour: an exit other than 0 or 1 on the head without the batch (collection error, no tests, timeout counted as red
without kinds) gives "owned": the ticket is ejected, though the batch may be innocent. The branch is kept and the CTO sees
the line; nothing is lost.
Ordinary work: yes, because a loaded machine or a broken head tree can hit it in a landing.
Consequence: other (fails closed: an ejection, work kept on its branch)
Scope: in (Q-1), not blocking; the same as the earlier trace_node rule.

```verdict
{"kpis": [{"kpi": "Q-1", "verdict": "pass", "findings": [{"id": "F2", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "no", "consequence": "fails open"}, {"id": "F3", "scope": "out", "ordinary_work": "no", "consequence": "fails open"}, {"id": "F4", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "yes", "consequence": "other"}]}, {"kpi": "G-1", "verdict": "pass", "findings": [{"id": "F1", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "no", "consequence": "fails open"}]}]}
```
EOF
